Schwann internode vs nonmyelinating support, lipid extraction, clefts/nodes, connective sheaths, perineurial tight junctions and regrowth guidance match. Direct primary PDF193 independently extracted.

previous.subject: histology
previous.prompt: After damage to an articular surface, a repaired region contains predominantly dense type I collagen-rich tissue with few cells. Which conclusion is best supported histologically?

options.text: Normal hyaline cartilage has necessarily regenerated because a collagen matrix is present
The repaired region must be lamellar bone because its matrix contains type I collagen
The region is elastic cartilage because elastic and collagen-rich repair tissue are histologically equivalent
The defect has acquired fibrous repair tissue, without demonstrating restoration of normal hyaline cartilage

previous.explanation: Repair of cartilage can be slow and incomplete and may yield fibrous tissue. Dense type I collagen-rich tissue does not reproduce the organized type II collagen-proteoglycan matrix with chondrocytes of a normal articular surface.

distractorExplanations.A: Collagen type, organization and cell phenotype matter; merely detecting collagen cannot establish restoration of hyaline cartilage.
distractorExplanations.B: Bone requires additional evidence such as mineralized matrix organization and osteocytes; type I collagen alone is insufficient.
distractorExplanations.C: Elastic cartilage requires chondrocytes and an elastic-fiber network. Collagenous repair tissue does not establish those features.

previous.learningObjective: Distinguish collagenous repair tissue from restoration of an organized hyaline articular surface.

reviewed.subject: histology
reviewed.prompt: After damage to an articular surface, a repaired region contains predominantly dense type I collagen-rich tissue with few cells. Which conclusion is best supported histologically?

options.text: Normal hyaline cartilage has necessarily regenerated because a collagen matrix is present
The region is established mature fibrocartilage solely because type I collagen is abundant
The collagen-rich repair necessarily restores the original compressive behavior of the articular surface
The defect has acquired fibrous repair tissue, without demonstrating restoration of normal hyaline cartilage

reviewed.explanation: Repair of cartilage can be slow and incomplete and may yield fibrous tissue. Dense type I collagen-rich tissue does not reproduce the organized type II collagen-proteoglycan matrix with chondrocytes of a normal articular surface.

distractorExplanations.A: Collagen type, organization and cell phenotype matter; merely detecting collagen cannot establish restoration of hyaline cartilage.
distractorExplanations.B: Fibrocartilage requires a cartilage component with chondrocytes and corresponding matrix; type I collagen abundance alone cannot establish that tissue identity.
distractorExplanations.C: The presence of collagenous repair does not establish restoration of the original hyaline cartilage architecture or its mechanical properties.

reviewed.learningObjective: Distinguish collagenous repair tissue from restoration of an organized hyaline articular surface.
